mutants.description: The saturation hold takes precedence over pwm_rise, so a rising edge seen while period_counter is saturated neither captures prev_period nor restarts the counter.
mutants.reason: After pwm_sync stalls for more than 255 clocks and then switches again, period_counter stays at all-ones for good and prev_period is never updated, where the original captures all-ones and starts measuring again on the first rise.

mutants.description: pwm_fall is handled before the saturation hold, so a falling edge on a saturated counter takes the normal fall branch and increments the counter past all-ones.
mutants.reason: When pwm_sync stalls high long enough to saturate and then falls, period_counter wraps to 0. The next rise then captures a short prev_period instead of the all-ones out-of-range marker.

mutants.description: Saturation applies only while PWM is high (the stall-high case named in the comment), and a stall with pwm_sync held low is forgotten.
mutants.reason: If pwm_sync stays low for more than 255 clocks, period_counter wraps to 0 and the next rise captures a small prev_period instead of all-ones.

mutants.description: The counter saturates at the nominal period CLKS_PER_SW (111) instead of the counter's all-ones limit, which forgets the drift headroom CNT_W was sized for.
mutants.reason: When the oscillator drifts slow enough that a period is longer than about 112 clocks, period_counter freezes at 111. prev_period (and duty_count, if the fall comes late) are clipped to 111 instead of showing the true count, and a stall reads 111 instead of all-ones.

mutants.description: duty_count is cleared at the start of every switching period as if it were run state, but it is a held snapshot that should keep the last high-phase length.
mutants.reason: In every period, duty_count reads 0 from the clock after pwm_rise until the next pwm_fall. During that window it no longer holds the last high time, and it is no longer consistent with prev_period.

mutants.description: prev_period adds one for the rise clock, so the period is counted differently from duty_count, which is taken from the same counter run without the +1.
mutants.reason: Every captured prev_period is one higher than the original. After a stall the saturated all-ones value wraps to 0, so a dead modulator reads as a zero-length period instead of the out-of-range marker.

mutants.description: PWM polarity misremembered as active-low: the switching period is taken from falling edge to falling edge and the duty snapshot is taken on the rising edge, so duty_count measures the low (LS) phase instead of HS conduction.
mutants.reason: For any running PWM with duty other than 50%, duty_count reports the low-phase length (period minus high time) instead of the high-phase length; prev_period stays about the same, so the host infers the wrong Vout.

mutants.description: The start-of-cycle detector fires on any PWM edge rather than only the rising edge, so the period counter is restarted at the end of HS conduction as well.
mutants.reason: With a running PWM, prev_period alternately captures the high-phase and the low-phase length instead of the full period, and duty_count is never updated by a normal falling edge because the restart branch wins.

mutants.description: A rising edge that ends a saturated (stalled) period is treated as invalid and does not update prev_period, so the all-ones out-of-range marker is never exported.
mutants.reason: After pwm_sync stalls long enough for period_counter to saturate and then resumes, prev_period keeps the last plausible period instead of reading all-ones, hiding the stall from the host.

mutants.description: The saturation test looks ahead at the next count, so the period counter stops one short at all-ones minus one instead of reaching the all-ones out-of-range marker.
mutants.reason: When pwm_sync stalls for more than 254 clocks, the following rising edge exports prev_period = 0xFE (and a fall exports duty_count = 0xFE) instead of the all-ones value the host recognises as out-of-range.

mutants.description: When a stalled-high PWM finally falls, the saturated period counter is restarted at the fall as if measurement had recovered, rather than held until the next rising edge.
mutants.reason: After a stall-high long enough to saturate the counter, the next rising edge exports only the low-phase length as prev_period, a plausible short period, instead of the all-ones marker for the stalled cycle.

mutants.description: The duty snapshot is taken on the PWM low level instead of on the falling edge, so duty_count keeps being overwritten throughout the low phase.
mutants.reason: For a running PWM, duty_count follows period_counter during the whole low phase and ends near the full period length at the next rise, instead of holding the high-phase length captured at the fall.

mutants.description: The falling-edge clock is counted as part of HS conduction, so duty_count is one higher than the count taken from the same counter run for prev_period.
mutants.reason: For every normal period, duty_count reads one count higher than the high-phase length on the same basis as prev_period, so duty/period is biased high and reads 100% duty one count early.

mutants.description: The saturation test reads the extra drift-headroom MSB as an overflow flag, so the period counter stops at 2^(CNT_W-1) (128) instead of the all-ones out-of-range marker.
mutants.reason: If pwm_sync stalls high or low for more than 128 clocks, prev_period (and duty_count, if it stalled high) reads 128 instead of 255 after the stall. The host then sees a plausible long period, not the all-ones marker.

mutants.description: The prev_period snapshot is copied into the falling-edge branch too, so the period export is overwritten at the end of HS conduction as well as at the start of the cycle.
mutants.reason: In the low phase of every switching cycle, prev_period equals duty_count (the high-phase length) instead of the previous full period. It is corrected only at the next rising edge, so a read during the LS phase gets a wrong switching period.

mutants.description: The period counter is gated by the PWM level, as if it were an on-time counter, so it stops during the LS phase and does not span the whole switching period.
mutants.reason: In any cycle with a low phase longer than one clock, prev_period is captured at the next rise as roughly duty_count+1 rather than the full period. A stall with pwm_sync held low also never saturates to the all-ones marker.

mutants.description: The drift-headroom MSB of the period counter is treated as internal only and is dropped from the prev_period export, so the exported period is taken modulo 2^(CNT_W-1).
mutants.reason: When pwm_sync stalls and the counter saturates, the next rising edge exports 127 instead of the all-ones out-of-range marker 255. Any slow period of 128 or more clocks also reads short, which looks like a higher switching frequency.

mutants.description: The saturation hold is applied only to a stall with pwm_sync held low (a dead modulator taken to mean PWM low). The stalled-high case named in the comment is left out, so the counter wraps.
mutants.reason: If pwm_sync stays high for more than 255 clocks, period_counter wraps through 0. The fall then captures a small duty_count and the next rise exports a short prev_period instead of all-ones.

mutants.description: The start-of-cycle strobe pwm_rise is registered, unlike pwm_fall, so the period counter is restarted one clock after the rising edge while the duty snapshot still uses the combinational fall.
mutants.reason: In steady switching, duty_count reads one less than the HS high time measured from the same counter run, so it no longer matches prev_period. With a one-clock HS pulse, the delayed rise and the fall land on the same clock, the rise wins, and duty_count is not updated.
after: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin

mutants.description: The out-of-range marker is published to prev_period as soon as period_counter saturates, mid-period, instead of when the next rising edge closes the stalled period.
mutants.reason: If pwm_sync stalls (high or low) long enough to saturate the counter, prev_period changes to all-ones during the stall instead of keeping the last complete period. In the original it changes only at the next rising edge, and never changes if no rising edge comes.

mutants.description: 'Both captured from the same counter run' is misread as 'both captured at the same rising edge', so duty_count is also loaded with the full period count at every rising edge.
mutants.reason: After each rising edge, duty_count equals prev_period (the whole switching period) until the next falling edge overwrites it. During the HS phase the host reads 100% duty, and if PWM stalls high it keeps reading that value.

mutants.description: The duty snapshot is assumed never to exceed the nominal period (111 < 128), so the drift-headroom MSB of period_counter is dropped from duty_count and the high-phase length is exported modulo 2^(CNT_W-1).
mutants.reason: When a stalled-high PWM finally falls with the counter saturated, duty_count reads 127 instead of the all-ones out-of-range marker 255. The same happens for any high phase of 129 or more clocks: duty_count reads short.

mutants.description: The out-of-range marker is made sticky: a rising edge that ends a saturated period captures all-ones into prev_period but does not restart period_counter, so the counter stays saturated until reset.
mutants.reason: After one stall (pwm_sync held high or low until period_counter reaches 255), the PWM can resume normally. prev_period then reads 255 at every later rising edge, and duty_count reads 255 at every later falling edge, until rst_n is asserted. It should show the real period and duty again.
